Let

\[ S = \sum_{k=0}^{2026} k \binom{2k}{k} 2^k. \]

Compute the remainder when \( S \) is divided by 2027. (Note that 2027 is prime.)

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). Work in \(\mathbb F_p\).

Define
\[
F(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \binom{2k}{k}x^k.
\]
We claim
\[
F(x)=(1-4x)^m \pmod p.
\]

For \(m<k<p\), Lucas’ theorem gives
\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv \binom{1}{0}\binom{2k-p}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p,
\]
since \(2k-p<k\). Thus those coefficients vanish.

For \(0\le k\le m\), the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \((1-4x)^m\) is
\[
\binom{m}{k}(-4)^k
=\prod_{j=1}^k \frac{-4(m-j+1)}{j}.
\]
Since \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}\),
\[
-4(m-j+1)\equiv 4j-2 \pmod p,
\]
so
\[
\binom{m}{k}(-4)^k
\equiv \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{4j-2}{j}
=\prod_{j=1}^k \frac{2(2j-1)}{j}
=\binom{2k}{k}.
\]
Hence \(F(x)=(1-4x)^m\).

Now
\[
S=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} k\binom{2k}{k}2^k
=\left[xF'(x)\right]_{x=2}.
\]
Since \(F(x)=(1-4x)^m\),
\[
xF'(x)=-4mx(1-4x)^{m-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
S\equiv -8m(-7)^{m-1}\pmod p.
\]

By Euler’s criterion,
\[
(-7)^m\equiv \left(\frac{-7}{p}\right).
\]
Now
\[
\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)
=\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right).
\]
Since \(2027\equiv 3\pmod 4\), \(\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)=-1\). Also \(2027\equiv 4\pmod 7\), and by reciprocity,
\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)=-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)=-\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)=-1.
\]
Therefore \(\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)=1\), so \((-7)^m\equiv 1\). Hence
\[
(-7)^{m-1}\equiv (-7)^{-1},
\]
and
\[
S\equiv -8m(-7)^{-1}\equiv \frac{8m}{7}\pmod p.
\]
Since
\[
8m=8104\equiv -4\pmod{2027},
\]
we get
\[
S\equiv -4\cdot 7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]
The inverse of \(7\) modulo \(2027\) is \(1448\), because \(7\cdot 1448\equiv 1\). Thus
\[
S\equiv -4\cdot 1448\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
